entries.title: Export audit logs to your SIEM
entries.summary: a new **Audit log export** permission on API tokens creates a token your security team uses to pull API request, security and audit logs into Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic or another SIEM. It reads logs only, always covers the whole organization, and can be created by users who manage users. Failed API sign-ins are now logged with the reason.

enable.path: Org Settings → API tokens → create a token with the Audit log export permission

entries.use_case: Security teams at enterprise and association customers ask for log export during procurement and SOC reviews. A read-only, org-wide token feeds Splunk, Sentinel or Elastic without giving the API any other access.

cs_action.note: Mention in security questionnaires and renewal conversations with IT stakeholders.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Security review, SSO rollout, enterprise renewal, any 'do you have audit logs' question.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise, Informa, any customer with a security team.
internal.gotchas: Needs the manage-users permission to create the token. Failed API sign-ins are now logged with the reason.

entries.title: Sites: Rooms layout for the Agenda page
entries.summary: the Agenda page's **Layout** gains **Rooms**: one column per room, sessions stacked by time, a tab per day, the room's capacity under its name when you have set one, and an **Unassigned** column for sessions without a room. Rooms follow the order from **Program → Settings → Locations**. Like the Agenda grid, it needs the Location field on.
entries.use_case: A room-by-room grid with capacity and an Unassigned column is what multi-track programs want on their public agenda, and it follows the Locations order already set in Program settings.

internal.gotchas: Needs the Location field on, like the Agenda grid.

entries.title: Sites: Countdown block
entries.summary: a new block under **Marketing** counts down to one exact moment and prints the date in your event's time zone. Pick **Tiles**, **One line** or **Badge**, add a label, hide the seconds, set what it says once the moment passes, and add a button. It starts on your event's start date; **Use event start** puts it back.

enable.path: Site builder → add block → Marketing → Countdown

where.path: CMS → Sites → page builder → Marketing blocks

entries.use_case: A countdown to the CFP deadline or event start on the landing page, in the event's time zone, with a configurable post-deadline message and button.

entries.title: Sites: your own domain (limited release)
entries.summary: a Site can be served from a domain you own, such as `events.example.org`, with pages at the root and your domain alone in the address bar, search results and share cards. Connecting is handled with your Customer Success Manager for now: you add a CNAME and a TXT record, and the Site goes live on the new address once the certificate is issued. Marketing-layout pages are indexable with canonical links, schema.org `Event` data and a `sitemap.xml` on your domain.

enable.path: Handled with your Customer Success Manager: add a CNAME and a TXT record; the Site goes live once the certificate issues

entries.use_case: The event site lives at events.example.org — the customer's domain in the address bar, search results and share cards — which is the single most common objection from marketing teams to a hosted site.

cs_action.note: CSM-led setup; collect the domain, send the DNS records, confirm the certificate issued.

internal.staff_path: Settings → Domains → site domains (staff-only tab) — see web-ui-v2 #867
internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Site conversation with a marketing team; competitive deals against website builders.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sites as their public event website; Informa brands.
internal.gotchas: Marketing-layout pages are indexable with canonical links and a sitemap on the customer's domain.

entries.title: v1 / v2 badges on forms and evaluation plans
entries.summary: every submission form and evaluation plan now shows a **v1** or **v2** badge, with a **Version** filter and a count of what is still on v1, so you can see what to convert before an event's 60-day lock applies. Your Customer Success Manager can unlock v1 editing for an event when converting is not an option; the list then says so.

where.path: Forms list and Evaluation plans list → v1 / v2 badge, Version filter

entries.use_case: Customers can see exactly what is still on the older builder before an event's 60-day lock applies, and plan conversions instead of discovering a locked form.

cs_action.note: CS can unlock v1 editing for an event when converting is not an option; the list then says so.

internal.staff_path: Admin Settings → Event → unlock v1 editing
internal.when_to_bring_up: Every renewal and pre-event check: how many v1 forms/plans are left?
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone with forms or plans built before 2026.
internal.gotchas: The 60-day lock is per event; cloned events convert to v2 automatically.

entries.title: Cloned events come out on v2
entries.summary: cloning converts v1 submission forms and v1 evaluation plans on the copy (the originals are untouched) and turns on the Embeds 2.0 builder; v1 plans that use personas are copied as-is and keep their **v1** badge.
entries.use_case: Cloning is the natural moment to leave the old builders behind: forms and evaluation plans on the copy come out on v2 and Embeds 2.0 is on, with the originals untouched.

cs_action.note: Tell customers cloning for next year that the copy will be on v2; persona-based v1 plans are copied as-is.

entries.title: Welcome survey: revisit a section after submitting
entries.summary: opening a section link of a submitted welcome survey now shows that section read-only, with **Back to summary**, instead of landing on the summary every time.
entries.use_case: A submitted welcome survey can be re-read section by section.
